THE CONTROL PRINCIPLE

The agent requests. Aegis decides.

The agent never receives unrestricted settlement authority. Every request passes through an external, deterministic policy engine.

01

Approve

Intent matches its task, recipient, amount and active policy.

02

Hold

Valid intent enters a settlement queue for final revalidation.

03

Block

A policy violation stops at the enforcement layer, not inside the agent.

04

Freeze

The owner revokes future and unsettled transaction authority instantly.

WHY AEGIS IS DIFFERENT

It does not trust the agent to obey.

Controls live outside the agent, so a buggy, compromised or overzealous system cannot simply ignore them.

01

Task-bound money

Funds are limited to an explicit purpose, approved vendors and expiry.

02

Adaptive defence

Permissions tighten automatically as behaviour becomes suspicious.

03

Evasion awareness

Related transactions are evaluated as a coordinated sequence, not isolated requests.

04

In-flight control

Pending intents are revalidated and can be revoked before settlement.

05

Policy simulation

Teams can prove a control works before enforcing it.

06

Forensic proof

Every approval, block and freeze is evidence-backed and replayable.

TECHNICAL PROOF

Enforcement you can inspect.

Every demo decision comes from the same deterministic engine and is preserved as replayable evidence.

LAYER 1

Aegis Risk Engine

Explains why an autonomous request should be allowed, held or blocked.

  • Behaviour monitoring
  • Task intent
  • Evasion Shield
  • Adaptive Risk Governor
  • Explainable decision evidence
SAME ATTACK VECTORS
LAYER 2

Aegis Policy Wallet

Independently enforces who may request and whether test-token settlement may execute.

  • Owner / agent separation
  • Allowlisted recipients
  • Transaction + cumulative limits
  • Permanent nonce protection
  • Two-phase settlement
  • Freeze + version invalidation
